title: Sentinel perception benchmark — local Apple Silicon CPU, FP32, whole clip
record_note: Values copied verbatim from the `runs[0]` object of `python -m app.benchmark --video <clip> --device cpu --frames 2100 --json`. Nothing is rounded, derived or filled in here. The run's own wall-clock timestamp is not carried by the harness output, so `run_timestamp` is null and `recorded` is the date this record was written. The clip's absolute path was a home directory and is omitted; the file name is kept.

companion_record.relationship: Same machine, same clip, same model and settings; a different measurement window. That record measures the harness default of 120 frames — the opening seconds. This one reads the whole 2105-frame clip. Both stand on their own; neither supersedes the other and no ratio between them is computed here.

comparison_note: One device. No second device was benchmarked, so this record contains no speedup, no parity check and no cross-device comparison of any kind. It is not related to, and must not be read against, the separate AMD MI300X record.

accelerator.mps_note: Apple Metal was available on this host and deliberately not used: the run requested `cpu` and the harness verified execution on the CPU.

workload.classes_note: null means no class filter — all COCO classes were kept.

clip.name: Screen Recording 2026-09-29 at 09.48.17.mov
clip.coverage_note: The whole clip was read: 2105 frames, of which the first 5 were warmup and discarded, leaving 2100 measured.

host.not_recorded_note: The harness reports the CPU architecture (`arm`) and core count, not the chip name or machine model. Neither is inferred here.

timing_note: Over 2100 frames the distribution has a long tail the 120-frame window did not reach: inference p50 16.899 ms against a max of 100.333 ms, and pipeline p50 18.361 ms against a max of 102.424 ms. The cause was not captured by the harness and is not guessed at here. Read p50 and p95 for typical cost and the max for the worst frame observed.
caveats: Not a general real-world performance claim: one clip, one host, one model, one resolution, single stream.
Not an accelerated result: CPU only. No MPS, no ROCm, no CUDA, no FP16, no INT8, no quantization, no batching, no ONNX Runtime or TensorRT.
Not a comparison: a single device was benchmarked, so no speedup or parity figure exists in this record.
Not a detection-accuracy result: the counts here are what the detector produced on this clip, with no ground truth to score them against.
Not interchangeable with the 120-frame record: same machine and clip, different window, and the content the two windows cover differs.
